rationale: Purging cash from the growth selector is a legitimate and previously untested identification fix (the issuance proceeds mechanically sit inside the archive's selector), and it is the only proposal here whose change is motivated by construction rather than taste — though the resulting composite still stacks three well-known anomalies (asset growth, net share issuance, cash holdings) and the supporting appeal to IssuanceIntoCashNotCapex is a loose reading of a differently-constructed signal.

Swapping the coverage denominator from total liabilities to interest-bearing debt is a cosmetic parameter change in a gate the archive has already shown to be insensitive to three numerator variants (all producing ~-0.045 alpha), and it introduces an undefined/exploding ratio for debt-free firms that will selectively drop the least-constrained population rather than rank it.

This simply bolts the TS_MIN persistence device already tested in EveryYearIssuerExpansion onto the non-cash growth selector of Proposal 1, changing two things at once in a family that already contains a multi-year expansion variant (MultiYearCapacityProgramOnOutsideMoney), so it adds no new mechanism and confounds attribution.

Replacing the issuance-quantity channel with per-share book value accretion is the one proposal that genuinely moves the funding leg away from the published net-issuance anomaly, but the archive's generation-1 slope (fmb -1.55 with the opposite expected sign) already leans against this direction, book equity per share is ill-behaved for negative-equity firms, and there is a real risk the result is just the cash gate re-expressed with an RMW-like tilt.

The debt version of exactly this conjunction (BorrowedDistributionsWhileExpanding) already failed with the wrong-signed alpha, and the equity version's high-scoring population — cash-poor, growing, dividend-paying issuers — is largely REITs and utilities, so the signal is more likely a sector-composition proxy than a measure of externally financed distributions.

A one-function wrapper is a thin "signal," but the attribution question it settles is the right one and directly addresses the standing concern that the cash/liabilities gate sorts on permanent industry type; it is worth running as a diagnostic, with the understanding that a surviving alpha is a robustness result rather than a new mechanism.
